title: Pupil's marked test paper and feedback
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Writing to argue and persuade; end of year
source: Seeded from english/y8 lesson 79 (Pupil's marked test paper and feedback (portal))
intro: Test. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.q: What links Squealer and Mark Antony?
options: both use persuasive language to move a crowd
questions.a: A) both use persuasive language to move a crowd. Both are skilled persuaders who change how a crowd thinks.

questions.q: Q5 is worth 12 marks. What must you do?
options: give your view and support it with evidence from the text
questions.a: B) give your view and support it with evidence from the text. An evaluation question needs a judgement backed by evidence.

questions.q: Which plan is strongest for Task A?
options: Clear view; three PEEDL points; a counter-argument; conclusion
questions.a: C) Clear view; three PEEDL points; a counter-argument; conclusion. A plan with a position, points and a counter-argument gives the article structure.

questions.q: What is the speaker's position?
questions.a: A) the greatest leaders serve. The final sentence states the position clearly.

questions.q: Which is the most arguable position?
options: Pupils should elect their class leaders every term.
questions.a: B) Pupils should elect their class leaders every term.. An arguable position is one people could disagree with.

questions.q: Which sentence DEVELOPS the point 'Elections are fairer'?
options: Over time, this builds trust in the leaders.
questions.a: C) Over time, this builds trust in the leaders.. Develop pushes the idea further, here to a long-term consequence.

questions.q: write a paragraph connecting one theme across two of the year's texts
questions.a: A connected paragraph with evidence from both
questions.model: Point: Both texts show how words can be used as weapons. | Evidence: Squealer's speeches; Antony's 'honourable man' | Explain: each persuader turns the crowd | Link: power belongs to those who control language

questions.q: write your time plan for each section of the test
evaluate which persuader, Squealer or Antony, is more dangerous, and why
Complete the retrieval quiz in the portal (15 questions)
questions.model: Teacher reads question 1 aloud and models a brief answer: 'What is Animal Farm an allegory of?' The Russian Revolution.

questions.q: Self-mark and note your two weakest texts
questions 1 to 4
questions.model: No model during the test. Plan: Q1 to Q3 quickly; Q4 about 13 minutes.

questions.q: question 5
check each answer answers its question
Practice before the timer: underline the key word in each question
questions.model: Teacher shows: Q4 key words: language, persuade.

questions.q: write your chosen task in the portal response box
questions.a: Marked with the mark scheme: content and organisation 18, accuracy 12
questions.model: No model during the test; models are shared in feedback (lesson 80).

questions.q: proofread (4 minutes)
upgrade two words
Plan (5 minutes): bullet plan for your chosen task
questions.model: Teacher reminder only: argue: position, 3 points, counter, conclusion; describe: senses, viewpoint, one change of focus.

questions.q: in the portal response box, explain how the speaker persuades, using three methods. Starter: 'The speaker persuades by...'
questions.a: Three methods with evidence and effects
questions.model: Point: The speaker persuades by involving the audience. | Evidence: 'Look around this room' | Method: direct address | Effect: each listener feels the speech is about them

questions.q: compare the speech with Brutus's or Antony's approach
suggest how the speech could appeal to reason more strongly
questions.a: For example: add an example or statistic

questions.q: Find the rhetorical question
questions.a: When you lead, will you rule, or will you serve?
questions.model: I do: look for a question that does not expect a spoken answer.

questions.q: Explain the effect of 'feared and forgotten'
questions.a: the alliteration and contrast make ruling by fear sound empty

questions.q: choose your speech topic on leadership and power and write a full introduction: hook, context, position, preview
questions.model: Labelled model: Hook (question) | Context (why now) | Position (arguable thesis) | Preview (three reasons)

questions.q: write two alternative hooks and choose the stronger
make your position more precise by adding a 'because' clause
Write a hook for a speech on leadership
questions.a: For example: Think of the best leader you have ever known.
questions.model: I do: speak to the audience with a question or instruction that makes them think of their own experience.

questions.q: write two PEEDL paragraphs for your speech
questions.model: Point: Firstly, ... | Evidence: ... | Explain: This shows... | Develop: Over time, ... | Link: That is why...

questions.q: strengthen one paragraph with a precise example or statistic you can check
vary your discourse markers (Firstly, Moreover, Crucially)
